tools.name: connect_account
tools.description: Connect the user's Marta account via BROWSER sign-in (no config files, no key copying). Two-phase: the FIRST call returns a link — show it to the user and ask them to open it and click Approve; once they say they did (or right away, it also waits ~60s), call this tool AGAIN to collect the key, which is stored in ~/.marta. Run whenever the account isn't connected. [free]

tools.name: configure_output
tools.description: Set where all marketing outputs are saved (run once; default ~/Documents/marketing-agent). Projects are <base>/<brand>/<campaign>/.

base_dir.description: absolute path or ~/… where outputs live

tools.name: get_balance
tools.description: Current credit balance + the per-tool price list. 1 credit = $0.01. Local-compose tools are free.

tools.name: top_up
tools.description: Add credits to the balance via Stripe checkout (TEST mode) — returns a link to open. Pick a pack (starter / studio / agency); the live pack sizes and prices come from the API and are listed back with the checkout link. Call get_balance or estimate to see current pricing before buying.

tools.name: estimate
tools.description: Estimate the credit cost of a generation tool before running it (for confirm-before-spend). For generate_voiceover, pass the exact script character count for an exact quote.

characters.description: script character count; used by generate_voiceover's exact length-based price

tools.name: init_project
tools.description: Scaffold a campaign project: <base>/<brand>/<YYMMDD_HHMM>_<campaign>/ (date-stamped so runs sort chronologically) with refs/, out/{explorations,grid,stills,video} — plus a brand-level brand_identity/ shared across campaigns. Direction samples go to out/explorations/; the grid + its IG feed mockup (preview.png) to out/grid/. Does NOT create brief.md/campaign.md (you author those with Write); use the returned paths for everything, and it returns a brief skeleton to fill in.

tools.name: set_brand
tools.description: Store/update a brand's kit (palette, accent/ink/paper, fonts, voice, positioning) in brand_identity/. Reused on every generation for on-brand output. Also stores an optional STYLE ANCHOR (one canonical reference image) + a FROZEN guidance line — both auto-reused on every generation so the whole feed shares one look (the biggest lever for cohesion).

voice.description: narration voice for UGC — one from list_voices

style_anchor.description: path or URL to ONE canonical style-reference image (ANY medium — a photo, an illustration, a 3D render). Auto-attached as a ref on EVERY generation so the whole feed shares one look. The single biggest lever for cohesion.

style_guidance.description: a frozen art-direction line applied to every generation (medium, palette discipline, mood). Kept identical across tiles so the look never drifts.

tools.name: add_product
tools.description: Scrape a real product photo from a URL and store it in the brand identity by name (for product-faithful generation via refs).

tools.name: scrape_web_images
tools.description: Scrape real images off ANY web page a plain Fetch can't read (403 / JS-rendered) — product pack-shots, site/editorial/lookbook imagery, campaign shots, anything. A REAL headless browser that scrolls the gallery: this is to any website what scrape_instagram is to Instagram. ALWAYS use this to pull images from a site — do NOT hand-write a Playwright/Python scrape (only do that if this returns nothing after trying a more specific URL + match/limit). Saves the top N to out_dir; returns paths + extra candidate URLs. [free]

match.description: keep only image URLs matching this regex (e.g. a product slug) — filters out site chrome

tools.name: resolve_refs
tools.description: Resolve identity asset names (products/logos) to file paths, to pass as `refs` into generation.

tools.name: scrape_instagram
tools.description: Look at a brand's PUBLIC Instagram feed (recent posts + captions + bio) to GROUND the campaign in their real aesthetic AND their writing VOICE. Saves the images, a contact sheet (Read it for the visual aesthetic), and captions.md (the real captions — Read it to derive the brand's caption voice). Best-effort — IG rate-limits; if it returns nothing, fall back to the site + web search. [free]

out_dir.description: where to save — use the BRAND level, <base>/<brand>/brand_identity/instagram, so every campaign can reuse the feed

tools.name: generate_graphic
tools.description: Render one branded graphic. Give a `prompt` (freeform) OR a structured `spec` (a GraphicSpec) — prefer the `spec` for any TEXT-bearing post: exact strings render with perfect spelling, bbox places them, and style.medium HARD-LOCKS the medium so the look never drifts. `refs` = image paths to keep the EXACT real object (e.g. a product). If the brand has a STYLE ANCHOR set, it is auto-attached as a ref for a consistent, on-model look (pass no_anchor to skip it for this one render). Saves to out_path. [metered]

out_path.description: absolute path to write the PNG

brand.description: brand name → applies its kit (and its locked style anchor + frozen guidance)

spec.description: a structured GraphicSpec — renders TEXT far more reliably than a freeform prompt. Shape: { highLevel, style:{ aesthetics, lighting, medium, art_style, palette:[hex] }, background, objects:[{ desc, bbox }], texts:[{ text, desc, bbox, palette }] }. bbox = [top,left,bottom,right] in a 0–1000 grid. Put the EXACT strings in texts[].text (perfect spelling) and place each with bbox — split a long headline into SEPARATE texts[] blocks. Set style.medium ('photograph' | 'illustration' | '3d_render' | 'graphic_design' | 'painting') to HARD-LOCK the medium and stop drift; style.palette pins the colors.

no_anchor.description: skip the brand's locked style anchor for this one render

tools.name: generate_carousel
tools.description: Generate a multi-image CAROUSEL post (2–10 slides the viewer swipes) with a LOCKED shared style — ideal for a product lineup, before/after, step-by-step, or a tips list. Slides render in parallel into <out_dir>/slide_01.png…; the shared look comes from one `brand` + `guidance` applied to every slide (write each slide's `prompt` to match). If the brand has a STYLE ANCHOR set, it is auto-attached as a ref on every slide so the carousel stays on-model (pass no_anchor to skip it). Use for SOME feed posts where one image can't tell the story. [metered per slide]

slides.description: 2–10 slides; each a freeform prompt or a GraphicSpec

guidance.description: shared art direction applied to EVERY slide — this is the style lock

refs.description: reference images kept across slides (e.g. the product)

no_anchor.description: skip the brand's locked style anchor for this carousel

tools.name: start_batch
tools.description: Fire MANY generation jobs at once — ANY mix (generate_graphic, generate_voiceover, generate_ugc, animate_still, ken_burns, edit_image, generate_logo) — and get a job_id to monitor, so a whole wave renders in parallel while you STILL stream progress. Each item = { label, tool, args } where `args` match that tool's own schema. Returns { job_id, total }; then loop `batch_status` until finished=true. Use this for ANY wave of ≥2 generations (the grid, or a mixed reel+regens+animation wave) instead of firing N tool calls in one silent turn. [metered per underlying tool]

label.description: short human label, e.g. 'tile 3 — the capsule' or 'the UGC reel'

tool.description: the generation tool to run, e.g. 'generate_graphic' | 'generate_voiceover' | 'generate_ugc' | 'animate_still' | 'ken_burns'

args.description: the args for that tool (same shape as calling it directly)

tools.name: batch_status
tools.description: Monitor a start_batch. BLOCKS until the next job finishes (or ~45s heartbeat), then returns progress — done/total, each item's status + path, and the current credit balance. Pass since=<the done count you last saw> so it returns the moment there's something new; loop until finished=true. This is how you stream progress on a big parallel wave. [free]

since.description: the done count you last saw — returns as soon as done > since

tools.name: generate_logo
tools.description: Generate a vector logo/mark (→ SVG; optional brand palette). [metered]

tools.name: edit_image
tools.description: Edit an image by instruction (recolor, swap bg, add/remove). `refs` = extra objects to composite in. [metered]

tools.name: animate_still
tools.description: Generate plausible in-scene motion from a still. Use only when the subject can naturally move and the product can remain faithful; for rigid products, UI, furniture, architecture, typography, or camera-only motion, use ken_burns instead. Inspect for warping and impossible mechanics before delivery. [metered]

tools.name: list_voices
tools.description: The valid narration voices for generate_voiceover or a UGC brief's `voice`, each with a tone hint. ALWAYS pick a `voice` from this list (or reuse the brand's saved voice) — don't invent names, unknown ones are rejected. [free]

tools.name: generate_voiceover
tools.description: Generate narration audio only (no video) from a script. Returns an MP3 plus provider timestamps and normalized word timings so captions and i2v edits can be synced precisely. Pick `voice` from list_voices. Use previous_text/next_text for continuity across separately generated sections. [metered by script length]

text.description: script to narrate; up to 2,500 characters

voice.description: voice id from list_voices; defaults to Rachel

language.description: ISO 639-1 language code, e.g. en, es, fr

previous_text.description: preceding script context for consistent delivery; not spoken

next_text.description: following script context for consistent delivery; not spoken

tools.name: generate_ugc
tools.description: Render a full multi-segment UGC video from a brief (voiceover + b-roll/app/avatar segments, captions, music, end card). Prefer voiceover-led (no avatar). `brief.voice` must be one from `list_voices`. `brief.exportDir` = the project video dir. [metered — most expensive]

brief.description: a UGC Brief object (slug, product{name,appUrl,exportDir}, voice, hookText?, musicPrompt?, brand{accent,ink,paper}, captionStyle?, segments[]). May be passed as a JSON object or a JSON string.

tools.name: generate_campaign_film
tools.description: Assemble an approved product or campaign storyboard into a polished MP4 using brand styled title cards, real image or video assets, an optional terminal scene, and a CTA. You direct the narrative and pass its approved beats as JSON; this tool renders and cuts them deterministically. Do not treat terminal as a default. 16:9 by default; use 9:16 for a stories variant. Add a one line music brief for a scored film, or omit it for silence. [metered: ≈5 credits when music is on; silent films are free]

brand.description: brand name: applies its stored kit (palette, ink, paper, accent, fonts)

beats.description: Array<Beat> as a JSON array (or JSON string). Beat kinds: {kind:'title', lines:[..], style?:'paper'|'ink', durationSec} | {kind:'asset', path, caption?, durationSec} (image or video; images get a slow push-in, videos trim) | {kind:'terminal', lines:[{who:'you'|'agent'|'tick', text}], durationSec} (optional; only when terminal interaction belongs to the story) | {kind:'cta', lines:[..], durationSec}. Caps: total <= 120s, <= 14 beats, <= 12 terminal lines per beat.

music.description: one line music brief (tempo, mood, no vocals, ending); omit for a silent film (free)

tools.name: ken_burns
tools.description: Turn a still into a slow pan/zoom video (free ffmpeg).

tools.name: contact_sheet
tools.description: Montage a set of images into one labelled grid for QA review (free).

tools.name: instagram_mockup
tools.description: Render a set of posts as a realistic Instagram profile + grid (free).

avatar.description: path to the profile photo; if omitted, an `_avatar.*` next to the first image is auto-used (else a text-initials avatar)

tools.name: vectorize
tools.description: Trace a raster image into a scalable SVG (free).

tools.name: preview_in_feed
tools.description: Preview new post(s) inside the brand's REAL Instagram feed: the new image(s) become the NEWEST tiles (top-left), and the latest real scraped posts fill the remaining grid — so a 3-post drop shows as 3 new + 6 real. Use it (a) on EACH direction sample and (b) on the FINAL drop for out/grid/preview.png. **Pass `feed_dir` (the scrape's output folder, e.g. <base>/<brand>/brand_identity/instagram) and it uses the real files itself — do NOT hand-type feed image filenames (they are ig_01.jpg… and guessing them yields a broken preview).** [free]

new_posts.description: the new image(s), newest first — one direction sample, or every post of the final drop

feed_dir.description: PREFERRED: the folder scrape_instagram saved to; the tool globs its images (natural-sorted) to fill the feed. Use this instead of feed_images.

feed_images.description: fallback: explicit real IG post image paths, if not using feed_dir

avatar.description: path to the profile photo; if omitted, an `_avatar.*` in feed_dir (saved by scrape_instagram) is auto-used (else a text-initials avatar)

tools.name: instagram_login
tools.description: Log into Instagram ONCE in a browser window — the user signs in manually, we save the session locally so instagram_post can publish later. Per-brand: pass session_path = <base>/<brand>/brand_identity/ig-session.json. The same browser profile (saved beside that file, and auto-gitignored) is reused for every later post, so login and posting come from ONE consistent device — do NOT move or delete it. LOCAL only — credentials never leave the machine, never touch the API. Opens a visible browser; tell the user to complete login there. Also run this after any Instagram security check, to confirm the account is healthy and lift the automatic posting hold. [free]

tools.name: instagram_post
tools.description: Publish ONE post to Instagram — a single image, or 2–10 paths for a carousel. Requires a prior instagram_login. `caption` is optional: if omitted, it's pulled automatically from the campaign's out/grid/captions.json by matching filenames (so you never copy-paste). **NEVER publish a whole grid in one go.** Posting runs at human pace in a visible browser window (about a minute per post) and the account's own posting history is enforced in code: at least 20 minutes between posts, max 4 per 24h. Publish ONE post, let the user confirm it, then plan the rest for later — ideally a few hours or a day apart; tell the user that spacing is what keeps their account safe, it is not the tool being slow. If Instagram shows any security/verification screen the run stops immediately, does not retry, and automated posting pauses for 24h — relay that to the user verbatim and do NOT try again. Set dry_run=true to rehearse (uploads + fills the caption, stops before Share) — a dry run still opens a real session, so it is not free of risk and counts toward the spacing rails. Best-effort: Instagram changes its UI — verify in the app afterwards. LOCAL only (free). [free]

images.description: ONE post's image path(s), in order; 2–10 = carousel. Never pass a whole grid as separate rapid calls.

caption.description: the post caption; omit to auto-pull from captions.json

captions_file.description: explicit path to a captions.json; else auto-located next to the images

dry_run.description: true = upload + caption but DON'T share (rehearsal; still opens a real session)

min_spacing_minutes.description: minutes to wait since this account's last post. The 20 min minimum is a floor enforced in code: this can only RAISE the gap (e.g. 180 for a slower, safer cadence), never lower it — anything smaller is clamped back to 20.
